angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 534,993 km at 23.64 pc = 0.3 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 42.2930 +/- 0.0178 mas (same row, RUWE 1.16): 23.64 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.769 +/- 0.026 solar radii from Barros et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of HD 207496 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...673A...4B/abstract): 534,993 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.8 +/- 0.04 solar masses from Barros et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of HD 207496 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...673A...4B/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4819 +/- 94 K from Barros et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 207496 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...673A...4B/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Barros et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 207496 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...673A...4B/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/hd-207496.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.569, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
